title: Sicilian Defense: Taimanov and Kan
line: A pawn one step forward keeps Black flexible, and the queen watches the open file.

steps.text: Here Black pushed the pawn in front of the king one square before taking in the center.
Bring the knight out to attack the knight on d4. This is the Taimanov.

also.a7a6: That is the Kan, a close cousin: the same plan with the knight later. This lesson goes on with the knight.
also.g8f6: That also works. This lesson brings the other knight out first.

steps.text: The Kan is the close cousin: the pawn goes to a6 first, the knight waits, and the queen comes to c7 the same way.
Back to the Taimanov. Bring the queen to c7. She watches e5, and she will look down the file once your knight moves off it.
Push the pawn on a7 one square. It keeps White's knights off b5.
Move the knight to e5. It eyes the bishop on d3 and the square c4.
steps.after: White's pawn keeps your knights off g4.

steps.text: Bring the bishop to c5. It hits the knight on d4, which the bishop on e3 guards.
steps.after: Your knight and bishop stand on active squares, and your king is ready to castle.

summary: The Taimanov and the Kan keep Black's pawns flexible, put the queen on the open file and the pieces on active squares.
